item.title: ‘Fell short with the ball’: Shreyas Iyer reflects on India's defeat, praises Glenn Phillips
item.description: Shreyas Iyer admitted India fell short with the ball in the fourth T20I against New Zealand, while praising Glenn Phillips for his match-winning century in Auckland on Friday. India suffered an 87-run defeat after New Zealand piled up 259/7, powered by Phillips' 107 off 49 balls and Michael Bracewell's 65 off 25. The hosts then bowled India out for 172/9 to register their first win of the five-match series, making it 3-1. Reflecting on India's bowling performance, Iyer said: "I think we fell a bit short in our bowling to start with. Powerplay, especially in the third over, they got that momentum from there on." The India captain, however, was full of praise for Phillips, who struck six fours and 10 sixes in a stunning knock. "Exceptional knock by Glenn. Some phenomenal shots, which were like pure bliss. So kudos to him. He's been consistent throughout the series, so lot to learn from him," Iyer said. India will look to regroup ahead of the final T20I in Hamilton. Iyer said the team would review its performance and work on executing its plans better. "I feel that it's important to retrospect, see where we can actually bounce back, coming into Hamilton. So I personally feel that we can probably go back to the drawing board and see to it we analyse and try to execute to the best of our abilities in the next game," he said. Iyer also acknowledged that adapting to the ground dimensions had been a challenge for some players, particularly those experiencing such conditions for the first time. "Some of them, it's their first time playing on such grounds. So it takes a bit of time for them to adapt to the challenge. It's not that easy, I understand that," he said. However, he backed the team to learn from the experience, pointing to their performances in the first three matches. "The way they executed the first three games, it was magnificent, and yeah, this is just a learning curve. I feel that next time when they come here, they would probably have a better idea on how to go about their business. So a great learning curve, and hopefully we come back positive in the next game," Iyer added.

item.title: Kylian Mbappe chasing remarkable La Liga record against Racing Santander
item.description: Kylian Mbappe chasing remarkable La Liga record against Racing Santander Real Madrid superstar Kylian Mbappe has been in excellent form since the start of the season. He is coming off a brace in the Clasico against Barcelona last weekend. The Frenchman enjoyed a memorable moment at the Spotify Camp Nou , reaching 100 goals for Los Blancos while helping Jose Mourinho’s team reduce the gap to 3 points. According to Diario AS , Mbappe now has another remarkable milestone in his sights. Having scored against all 23 teams he has faced in La Liga , the 27-year-old has a chance to make it 24. Mbappe looking to extend extraordinary scoring record Since joining Real Madrid in 2024, Mbappe has scored 67 goals in 75 league appearances. Individually, his performances have always been exceptional. It is quite remarkable that every opponent he has faced in the league has conceded to him at least once. Malaga and Elche were the latest additions to the list this season. Mbappe had a brilliant El Clasico last weekend. (Photo by David Ramos/Getty Images) Racing are now set to become his 24th different La Liga opponent. Real Sociedad are the team that has suffered the most. The Basque club has conceded seven goals to the Frenchman, followed by Barcelona with six and Villarreal and Sevilla with five each. Mbappe comes into this game in excellent form, having scored 6 goals and provided 1 assist in his last 5 appearances. Mourinho increasingly dependent on Mbappe’s goals Mbappe has already scored 14 goals across all competitions this season. This includes 11 in La Liga , which sees him sit second in the Pichichi race. His importance to the team is underlined by the points Los Blancos would have dropped without him. Kylian Mbappe is on course for the Pichichi. (Photo by Mateo Villalba Sanchez/Getty Images) Without his goals, Mourinho’s team would have collected seven fewer league points and four fewer Champions League points. The Portuguese manager has enormous faith in his talisman, starting him in every match. He has also played more than any other player in the squad. Mbappe will be keen to extend his goalscoring streak against Racing Santander at El Sardinero on Sunday. Scoring against a 24th different opponent in the league would be a remarkable record, and it remains to be seen whether Mbappe reaches this milestone against Racing.

item.title: Karim Adeyemi’s impressive Barcelona numbers put him in line for Alaves start
item.description: Karim Adeyemi’s impressive Barcelona numbers put him in line for Alaves start Karim Adeyemi is reportedly in line for a starting place when Barcelona host Alaves at Spotify Camp Nou on Saturday, with Hansi Flick looking to inject fresh energy into his attack after consecutive defeats against Paris Saint-Germain and Real Madrid. According to SPORT , the German winger is expected to benefit from the changes being considered by the Barcelona manager ahead of a demanding run of three matches in eight days. The fixture against Alaves will be followed by a Champions League meeting with Aston Villa on Tuesday before Barcelona travel to the Metropolitano to face Atletico Madrid on November 8. Flick wants his players to rediscover the attacking intensity and consistency they demonstrated earlier in the campaign. On that note, Adeyemi’s pace and direct running could make him a valuable asset as Barcelona attempt to overcome an Alaves defence that will require different attacking solutions. Adeyemi emerges as an attacking option for Flick Adeyemi’s potential inclusion in the starting XI is a clear example of the impact he has made since joining Barcelona from Borussia Dortmund. Adeyemi is likely to start against Alaves. (Photo by Francisco Macia/Getty Images) In fact, it is crucial to note that Adeyemi has featured in all 13 matches played by Barcelona this season, accumulating more than 450 minutes across competitions. However, he has started only four of those encounters, making his contribution from the bench an important part of his early campaign. Barcelona’s attacking numbers show Adeyemi’s efficiency The strongest argument for Adeyemi’s involvement is his productivity relative to the minutes he has received. With four goals and three assists giving him seven direct goal contributions in approximately 452 minutes, he is contributing roughly every 65 minutes, placing him third among Barcelona’s players in this particular measure. Only Lamine Yamal and Raphinha have recorded better averages. Yamal’s 10 goals and 10 assists translate to a contribution every 55 minutes, while Raphinha’s 15 goals and three assists give him an average of approximately 44 minutes per goal contribution. Adeyemi has hit the ground running at Barcelona. (Photo by Fran Santiago/Getty Images) These numbers alone show how efficiently Adeyemi has used his opportunities despite playing considerably fewer minutes than Barcelona’s established attacking leaders. Flick preparing for a tough run The timing of all these events is quite significant given Barcelona’s upcoming schedule. Flick’s side face three demanding fixtures before the next international break, beginning with Saturday’s meeting against Alaves. The Champions League encounter with Aston Villa follows on November 3, before the trip to Atletico Madrid five days later. Understandably, managing the workload of the attacking players will therefore be an important consideration for the German manager.

item.title: Joe Thomas reveals why he turned down Peyton Manning and refused to leave the Browns
item.description: Photo by Nick Cammett/Diamond Images via Getty Images Joe Thomas has revealed why he refused to force a trade away from the Cleveland Browns, even when Peyton Manning personally tried to convince him to join the Denver Broncos. The former offensive tackle spent his entire 11-season NFL career in Cleveland, earning 10 Pro Bowl selections and six first-team All-Pro honours despite never winning a Super Bowl. Thomas admitted that the Browns’ struggles eventually made him question whether he could achieve his championship ambitions in Cleveland. However, his connection with the franchise remained too strong for him to demand an exit. Joe Thomas explains why he refused to force a trade to the Denver Broncos Speaking on The Dan Patrick Show , Thomas was asked whether he had ever considered requesting a trade away from Cleveland. “I never did,” Thomas said. “I was always happy in Cleveland. I always felt a great pride in building something special. I loved the franchise. And I wanted to do it there.” Thomas explained that winning a Super Bowl with the Browns would have meant more to him than chasing a championship elsewhere. However, the veteran acknowledged that his belief in the project began to fade during his 10th season, when Cleveland entered a significant rebuilding period. “Even after I’d broken down in year 10 and realized, we ain’t doing it. We’re not good enough. I’m fooling myself. We can’t do it here anymore,” he said. Despite that realisation, Thomas still wanted to leave a lasting legacy in Cleveland rather than force his way out. His loyalty was tested when the Broncos approached him ahead of the 2015 trade deadline. Denver were looking for protection for Manning, who was approaching the end of his career, and the quarterback personally contacted Thomas to discuss a potential move. Manning explained that Denver had a deal on the table but needed Thomas to tell the Browns’ general manager that he wanted to be traded. Thomas admitted the offer was difficult to turn down but refused to push for a move. “I am happy in Cleveland. I love it here. If a deal gets done on its own merit, great; if not, I’m not willing to try and force a trade,” he said. Denver went on to win the Super Bowl that season, while Thomas remained in Cleveland for two more campaigns before retiring in March 2018. Although he never lifted the Lombardi Trophy, Thomas chose loyalty to the Browns over the chance to pursue a championship alongside Manning. item.title: England get back on track with impressive win over United States
item.description: England bounced back from consecutive defeats to Canada with an impressive display against the United States to end the WXV Global Series on a high. The Red Roses ran in nine tries during a 55-12 victory with Claudia Moloney-MacDonald the star as she crossed the line on four occasions as England dominated proceedings in New Jersey. The defeats to Canada were the team’s first consecutive losses for the in a decade and head coach John Mitchell freshened up the side making six changes and left Ellie Kildunne on the bench until the 61st minute. Moloney-MacDonald led from the front and scored the opening try in the fifth minute before captain Meg Jones finished off a swift move to extend the lead and show why the world champions had previously accummulated a 41-Test unbeaten run. (AP) Props Mackenzie Carson and Maud Muir peppered the USA defence with aggressive runs and sweeping long passes created space for Moloney-MacDonald to run in three more tries. Mo Hunt made a blindside dart before the ball was threaded right where wing Mia Venner strolled over before Bryony Field completed a maul try. Maddie Feaunati charged through a gap created by the power of the Red Roses’ maul and the pack also had the final say when Sadia Kabeya muscled over. “We wanted to impose ourselves on the USA,” England captain Jones said. “They came off the back of some good wins, so we knew they had momentum. We had to stop that and that’s what we did. (Getty) “When we got into it we started keeping the ball, being patient and had good control. Everyone was a threat to the line. We became unstoppable and I think that’s where the tries came from. “Off the back of two losses, we just wanted to learn and we’ll continue to learn. We’ve got so much feedback from this tour. We’re going to review it like we always do, reflect, and see where we can keep growing because I know there’s so much growth in this team. “We’re hungry to be better and to perform better. We’re just unbreakable at this point, but we need to keep pushing and growing.” PA contributed to this report.

item.title: Arsenal still unsure on Saka as key injury question emerges
item.description: Arsenal still unsure on Saka as key injury question emerges Mikel Arteta has admitted Arsenal still do not have a clear picture of Bukayo Saka’s injury, with further checks needed before they can say how serious it is. Photo by Alex Grimm/Getty Images Mikel Arteta has revealed that Arsenal are trying to establish whether Bukayo Saka ’s tendon has been affected as they continue to assess the winger’s quad injury but that the player is keen to be back quickly. Saka will miss Sunday’s trip to Liverpool after being forced off against Bayern Munich , but Arsenal are still waiting for a clearer picture before putting a timescale on his return. Arteta’s latest update offered one potentially significant detail, although it is important not to turn that into a diagnosis the club have not yet made. “As I said, he needed another scan to see how the amount of fluid that was there was resolving, whether the tendon is touched and how badly it is touched,” Arteta said . Photo by Alex Grimm/Getty Images “That’s all fine, and afterwards we’ll know more about it. We want to have him as quick as possible. The player is desperate, he’s feeling much better than he was a few days ago.” Arteta was just as cautious when asked whether Saka would miss England ’s forthcoming international fixtures. “Again, I don’t know,” he said. “It looks like it, but we’ll have to wait and see next week,” he said. What Arsenal do know is that they will be without him at Liverpool. There are also questions over Noni Madueke ’s fitness, while Max Dowman is suspended. Christos Tzolis has returned to training and could give Arteta another option. For now, though, the bigger concern is Saka. Photo by Leonhard Simon/Getty Images

item.title: English wonderkid will be Liverpool's new right-back, he's special
item.description: English wonderkid will be Liverpool's new right-back, he's special An exciting English wonderkid will likely be Liverpool's next wonderkid and he is special. The Reds will be exploring their options in the right-back market for the next few years. There will be high hopes for Conor Bradley to return to action, and it remains to be seen just when exactly that is going to happen. It's likely that if anything Bradley will only return to partial training after the November international break. When he will actually be match fit is moot. The target is probably beyond the new year - the same as Hugo Ekitike. Although the Frenchman is privately targeting a return that's a bit more sooner - potentially as early as Boxing Day in December. Bradley's return will be a welcome boost but with the defender having been plagued by injuries, Liverpool cannot rely on him alone. Liverpool's plans for the right-back role There are strong speculations, and murmurs on social media about a possible return for Trent Alexander-Arnold. Liverpool would naturally love to have him back. However, the question must be asked at what cost? Both his wages and a potential transfer fee likely will be quite high. Is it worth the risk to bring him back, when he is so low on confidence and he's also not getting any younger either? Especially, since Ronald Araujo has done so well. The Uruguayan is settling into that right-back role and make it his own. In the process he has become a fan favourite at Anfield. Right now, many supporters would likely admit they would prefer to sign him over Alexander-Arnold. There's also Jeremie Frimpong, who offers a different kind of dimension in the role but is also very injury prone. Wonderkid Lewis John-Charles will be Liverpool's next right-back Most people will not be familiar with the Reds' exciting young right-back, Lewis John-Charles. But Andoni Iraola will be. The youngster actually spent the beginning of pre-season preparing with Liverpool's U21 squad and a handful of first-team players who had reported to the AXA Training Centre early. At the time Iraola was watching over them, and John-Charles, who has since become an England U16 international, will have caught the eye. The youngster is an all-action and dynamic right-back. His incredible work-rate and engine is pretty much tailor-made for how Iraola wants to play. Sure, he is still young at the moment but with Araujo and Bradley making the club's right-back role their own, there's no rush for him to break into the first-team just yet. Long-term, though, it's looking quite likely that he will be Liverpool's next right-back given he is by far and away the most talented player in his position in the academy.

item.title: 'We would win now!' - Chelsea star Emiliano Martinez makes bold claim about World Cup final defeat to Spain
item.description: FBL-WC-2026-MATCH104-ESP-ARG-FINAL - AFP Chelsea and Argentina goalkeeper Emiliano Martinez believes his nation would defeat Spain if they replayed their recent World Cup final today. Despite praising the Spanish players, the veteran shot-stopper remains confident that Lionel Scaloni's squad are currently the superior side following their extra-time heartbreak. Martinez confident in Argentina over Spain Martinez has reflected on Argentina's painful World Cup final defeat against Spain . The South Americans suffered a narrow loss when Torres scored the only goal of the game during extra time. However, the Chelsea goalkeeper remains incredibly confident in his national team. The 34-year-old insists that Argentina would emerge victorious if the two sides squared off again today. Speaking in an interview, Martinez offered a bold assessment of the current balance of power in international football. He believes Scaloni's men possess the quality to overturn that bitter result. Chelsea star praises Spanish opposition Martinez did not shy away from acknowledging the immense talent within the Spanish ranks. He admitted that Luis de la Fuente has built a formidable squad capable of challenging any opponent on the global stage. Despite that respect, the shot-stopper feels Argentina have the upper hand right now. He opened up about his feelings during a candid conversation with journalist Gaston Edul . "I knew the players of the Spanish national football team were very good," Martinez explained. "But, I don't know, I felt and feel currently that we beat them if we play now." Comparing Spain to France in 2022 The discussion then shifted to previous tournaments and the calibre of opponents Argentina have faced. Martinez famously helped his country win the 2022 World Cup in Qatar after a dramatic penalty shootout against France. When comparing the two European heavyweights, the goalkeeper admitted that the French side instilled more fear in him. He pointed to their previous tournament success and squad maturity as key factors. "France 2022 gave me more respect," Martinez concluded. "They had been world champions back then, and had a much better age and more experience in the final. I had more respect for them." Continuing his recovery from injury Martinez is currently sidelined following surgery for a fractured jaw - an injury sustained during the Blues' 2-0 victory over Everton . He remains focused on his recovery so that he can return to the squad as soon as possible.

item.title: One League, Two Sponsorship Rulebooks
item.description: One League, Two Sponsorship Rulebooks Lazio’s Polymarket shirt deal didn’t survive the summer. In August, the Rome club parted with the prediction-market company after Italian regulators blocked its website. Yet Serie A had signed its own Polymarket agreement only months earlier, and that partnership was aimed squarely at the United States. The same company could be ruled out on a Lazio shirt in Italy while appearing in the league’s American media. The difference lies in where each deal is meant to operate. Lazio’s Search for a Shirt Sponsor REGGIO NELL’EMILIA, ITALY – OCTOBER 27: Tijjani Noslin of S.S. Lazio celebrates scoring his team’s fifth goal during the Serie A match between US Sassuolo and SS Lazio at Mapei Stadium – Citta’ del Tricolore on October 27, 2026 in Reggio nell’Emilia, Italy. (Photo by Emmanuele Ciancaglini/Getty Images) Lazio agreed a two-season sponsorship with Polymarket in April 2026, reportedly worth around €19 million, with an option for another year. It was a significant deal for a club that had struggled to fill the front of its shirt. A March breakdown of Serie A shirt sponsorship earnings identified Lazio as the only club in the division without a main shirt partner. Inter and Milan, by comparison, were each receiving around €30 million annually from their respective arrangements. By July, the optimism had faded. Italy’s Customs and Monopolies Agency, known as ADM, had again blocked access to the platform, treating it as an unauthorised gambling operator. Keeping its branding on Lazio shirts had become difficult to reconcile with the Italian advertising rules. Why an American Deal Is Different FLORENCE, ITALY – NOVEMBER 22: General view inside the stadium Artemio Franchi during the Serie A match between ACF Fiorentina and Juventus FC at Artemio Franchi on November 22, 2025 in Florence, Italy. (Photo by Gabriele Maltinti/Getty Images) Italy’s Dignity Decree restricts advertising for gambling and betting with cash winnings, including sports sponsorship. Whether a prediction market belongs in that category has been central to the Polymarket dispute. The company’s description of its product as a prediction exchange didn’t prevent ADM from treating its Italian activities as unauthorised gambling. The United States has a separate regulatory system, and access to prediction markets can depend on the state and the product offered. Readers can see how these distinctions work in practice at CBS Sports Polymarket review , which outlines US eligibility requirements, location restrictions and promotional terms. Those conditions explain who may use the American platform, not whether Polymarket’s branding is permitted on a Serie A shirt in Italy. Italian clubs need more than assurances about a sponsor’s US operations. They also need to know whether the branding they sell is permitted at home. item.title: Barcelona midfield mainstay ‘extremely happy’ and has no intention of leaving amid Manchester United interest – Romano
item.description: Barcelona midfield mainstay ‘extremely happy’ and has no intention of leaving amid Manchester United interest – Romano Barcelona have one of the best midfields in Europe, with Hansi Flick having a plethora of options at his disposal. The Catalan club have at least two players for each midfield role, with the likes of Pedri, Rodri, Frenkie de Jong, Gavi, Marc Bernal, Dani Olmo and Fermin Lopez making up the roster. One midfielder who has attracted considerable attention from across Europe is Fermin Lopez. He was linked with a move to Chelsea a couple of summers ago and now finds Manchester United interested in him. However, according to Fabrizio Romano , Fermin has no intention of leaving Barcelona anytime soon. The 23-year-old is extremely happy at the Catalan club. Barcelona determined to keep Fermin Lopez Transfer expert Matteo Moretto revealed that Manchester United had made enquiries about signing both Fermin and Atletico Madrid’s Pablo Barrios. However, neither enquiry has led to formal negotiations, with both Spanish clubs having no intention of selling their respective midfielders. Everyone at Barcelona considers Fermin an important part of the project, and Hansi Flick trusts him to start big games. Fermin Lopez will not leave Barcelona amid Manchester United interest. (Photo by Burak Kara/Getty Images) Fermin’s position is equally clear. The La Masia graduate signed a contract until 2031 earlier this year and is keen on succeeding at Barcelona. The numbers explain why the club are so confident about him. Fermin has already scored five goals and provided four assists in 12 appearances this season. The 23-year-old has managed to reach these numbers despite frequently having to share minutes with Dani Olmo. Fermin becoming increasingly important for Flick However, Fermin’s importance to Hansi Flick’s team extends beyond just his goalscoring and assist numbers. His intelligent movement into the penalty area, aggressive pressing and ability to score from distance are invaluable qualities for Barça . Although Barcelona have several technically gifted midfielders, Fermin offers something completely different. Fermin Lopez is determined to succeed at Barcelona. (Photo by David Ramos/Getty Images) Barça have never been a club too keen on selling their academy graduates, and there is absolutely no reason to even consider a sale for the Spaniard. Fermin’s career shows that academy graduates don’t always have to be child prodigies to break into the first team. Manchester United’s interest shows just how highly clubs across Europe rate Fermin, and Barça should look to keep him for as long as possible.

item.title: Chelsea Starting XI vs Man United: Confirmed Team News and Predicted Lineup
item.description: Chelsea Starting XI vs Man United: Confirmed Team News and Predicted Lineup Chelsea Team News: Cole Palmer Returns, Maxence Lacroix Out for Manchester United Clash Chelsea go into the visit of Manchester United with one important boost and a familiar problem. Cole Palmer is available again after suspension, while Maxence Lacroix has joined the injury list after pulling up at Anfield in midweek. Palmer missed the Carabao Cup defeat to Liverpool after his red card against Tottenham. His return matters because Chelsea have lacked calm and incision in key moments, and he usually supplies both. Xabi Alonso gets one of his most decisive attackers back at the right time, with a demanding league fixture next at Stamford Bridge. Cole Palmer return lifts Chelsea There is no need to overcomplicate it. Chelsea are better with Palmer in the side. He gives structure to attacks, carries a threat between the lines and takes responsibility when games get messy. After a poor night in the cup, that sort of presence is required against a Manchester United side that will sense vulnerability. The bigger issue is at the back. Lacroix went off before half time against Liverpool with a hamstring problem, and Alonso made it clear the defender will be missing for a while. “Max, he picked up an injury, and we expect that he’s not going to be ready before the international break,” the Spaniard said. “So he will be a few weeks out.” Maxence Lacroix joins growing injury list Lacroix is the latest absentee in a squad that is already carrying too many of them. Reece James remains out until the new year after knee surgery. Joao Pedro is also unavailable, with Alonso saying: “He has an injury to his thigh, and he is going to be out for a few weeks. Let’s see how many. We don’t want to predict on that, but he is not ready for the next games.” Jorrel Hato and Jamie Gittens are still sidelined as well, while Malo Gusto and Moises Caicedo have come through recent issues and are fit to feature. Pep Chavarria is expected back in the squad, which at least gives Chelsea another option in a stretched group. Emi Martinez recovery offers Chelsea hope There is some encouragement in goal. Emi Martinez could return earlier than expected after surgery on a broken jaw. He has seen a specialist over a protective mask, and Alonso said: “Yes, there is a chance. We need to still wait for next week, but let’s see how things go. But there is a chance.” Predicted Chelsea XI: Penders, Acheampong, Colwill, Fofana, Neto, Caicedo, Henderson, Chavarria, Palmer, Rogers, Welbeck. For Chelsea, the equation is simple enough. Palmer is back, the injury list is still awkward, and Alonso needs a response after the cup exit. That is the state of play before Manchester United arrive.

Mourinho sends clear warning to Real Madrid players The manager wants his team to maintain the same intensity against Racing that helped them overcome Barcelona. “We have to go out to win and give everything,” Mourinho has told his squad. item.title: Oscar Piastri Leaves Mexico City FP2 Optimistic Despite ‘Pretty Messy' Qualifying Simulation
item.description: Oscar Piastri heads into FP3 with renewed confidence in the MCL40. (Source: MEGA) With the first day of practice sessions in Mexico City done and dusted, McLaren’s Oscar Piastri walked away from the circuit with optimism, despite a ‘messy’ qualifying simulation. Sitting at over 2,200 meters above sea level, the Autodromo Hermanos Rodriguez circuit is surrounded by thin air that leaves teams running with very little downforce and poor cooling. Facing this unique challenge, Piastri was pleasantly surprised at the way things ultimately panned out. While he agreed that the challenge was tough to overcome, the Australian admitted that the overall run was ‘a little better’ than he expected. The MCL40 surprised Oscar Piastri with its performance in Mexico City. (Source: MEGA) Speaking to the F1 media following a whole day of practice runs, the No. 81 driver further admitted: “My soft [tire] lap in FP2 was pretty messy, but I felt like the kind of overall pace seems to be there.” With low grip being the norm pretty much on every track this season, adapting to it, particularly for the Mexico City track, did not feel like a new challenge for him. Under the new regulations, low grip has become the norm in F1, and so it wasn’t a dramatic new change for him. However, Piastri feels that cooling the engine to an optimum temperature would prove difficult for all the teams. And away from it all, the Aussie driver sees Ferrari as the team to beat in Mexico. Oscar Piastri Tips the Balance in Favor of Ferrari but Not by Much While Piastri was happy to be driving the challenging MCL40 around the Mexico City track, his machine was still far from the pace that Ferrari had to offer. With Charles Leclerc topping both Friday sessions once again, the Australian driver had no issue admitting that the team in the scarlet red “looked very strong.” Oscar Piastri: "Mexico is always a challenge with the altitude, low downforce and very little grip, but today felt slightly better than I expected.
